description: Provenance of the process-table fixtures used by packages/core/test/process/tree. Bytes are stored exactly as produced (see .gitattributes).

fixtures.how: bash (pid 8) with job control started copies of /bin/sleep named 'a) (b c' (16), 'x) R 1 1 1 0' (17), 'nl<LF>9 1 9 Z' (18), bytes FF FE '-bad' (19), and bash -c (20, own group) running two 'plain' sleeps (22, 23); every /proc/<pid>/stat was copied byte for byte with cat. fixtures.how: LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC0 ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,stat=,lstart=,comm= (procps-ng; same column specification as the macOS command, parsed with dialect 'procps'). bash (pid 7) with job control started copies of /bin/sleep named 'a) (b c' (16), 'x) R 1 1 1 0' (17), 'nl<LF>9 1 9 Z' (18), bytes FF FE '-bad' (19); bash -c (20) started 'true' in the background and exec'd into a sleep named 'reaper', which never reaps it, so pid 21 is a zombie (stat Z); bash -c (22) running two 'plain' sleeps (22, 23). procps prints the newline of pid 18 as '.' and the invalid bytes of pid 19 as '?'. Everything ended on its own (sleep 6); nothing was signalled.

Get-CimInstance Win32_Process mapped to {p, pp, t = CreationDate.ToFileTimeUtc() as a string, n} and ConvertTo-Json -Compress, as specified on Win32CimTableCalls; filtered to pids 0 and 4, the recording PowerShell, its ancestors and its children so no unrelated process names are stored. The parent of explorer.exe had exited, so its ppid names a pid that is absent.
the single-object form that PowerShell 5.1 produces when the pipeline holds one object

Written by hand in the BSD layout of '/bin/ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,stat=,lstart=,comm=' under LC_ALL=C and TZ=UTC0: numbers right-aligned (width 5), stat left-justified (width 4), lstart '%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Y' left-justified in width 28 (4 padding spaces after the date), one space between columns, comm last (the executable path, or '(<p_comm>)' when ps cannot read the arguments). The lstart padding is confirmed by macOS gate run 1 (every parsed name carried exactly 4 extra leading spaces, research 09); the stat column is NOT yet recorded on macOS and the next gate run must confirm it (its raw ps lines are in the item 2 evidence). It also contains hostile cases: a name with spaces and parentheses, a forged line (pid 480 repeated, as a newline in a name could produce if ps did not escape it), an empty name, a zombie '(security)' (stat Z, the shape run 1 saw), a name with its own leading spaces, a stat with flag characters, a wrong weekday, a line with the procps gap and a malformed line.
